Governance, accountability, risk, ISMS and cyber strategy

NDIA must govern cyber security through approved roles, delegations, risk appetite, security planning, ISMS-aligned practices, cyber strategy and reporting that support accountable decisions and escalation of material cyber risks.

NDIA must assign clear cyber security responsibilities, maintain an ISMS-aligned governance model, set risk appetite, track cyber risks and report material issues to executives so decisions and escalations are clear.

2. Secure technology lifecycle, architecture and operations
Secure technology lifecycle, architecture, cloud, gateways and secure configuration

NDIA systems must be designed, built, procured, authorised, configured, changed and operated using secure architecture patterns, approved technology lifecycle controls, cloud and gateway safeguards, and secure configuration baselines proportionate to classification, data sensitivity and business risk.

NDIA must build security into every stage of the technology lifecycle. New or changed systems, cloud services and gateways must follow approved architecture, secure configuration and authorisation processes before they are used.
